title: Almost Every Fish Is Cold-Blooded. The Opah Isn't
subject: opah fish

scenes.text: Almost every fish is cold-blooded. This one isn't.
It's the opah. It dives below six hundred and fifty feet, where the water is under four degrees Celsius.
Yet its muscles run about five degrees warmer than the water around it.
The heater is its fins. It flaps them nonstop, and all that motion makes heat.
The gills keep the heat. Warm blood leaving the body warms the cold blood coming in.
A warm body means quicker reactions and sharper eyes. The opah hunts squid in the cold, and wins.

description:
Almost every fish is cold-blooded, but the opah isn't.
NOAA scientists found its muscles run about 5 degrees Celsius warmer than the water it hunts in, thanks to constant fin flapping and gills that recycle heat.
Would you have guessed a fish could do that?
first_comment: Which would you rather meet in the deep: an opah or a giant squid?
